prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, which brought optical frequency standards to the 10^-18 level of accuracy and stability

statement.case_for: I now propose B034 as a single-part prize and withdraw the B005 part from my round-1 configuration. The scientific case is unchanged and has been strengthened by the exchange. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the conflict between trapping many neutral atoms and perturbing the clock transition, and Ye's strontium clock took fractional uncertainty and stability to the 10^-18 regime. Independent national laboratories reproduce and compare clocks at that level, the interpretation is settled, and the clocks are used for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the preparation of a redefinition of the second. The two-name credit maps onto proposal and realisation without forcing any omission inside the credited set. Maturity is the best on the shortlist after B028 and does not depend on any pending administrative decision. As an instrumentalist I judge this as an invention in the sense of the Nobel will: a new method that enlarged what physics can measure.
statement.case_against: The strongest objections stand. The 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for quantum control of single ions cover neighbouring metrology territory, and I cannot claim the novelty argument is closed, only that the magic-wavelength lattice scheme is distinct from both. Other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Bloom) have defensible priority claims that a two-name credit leaves out, and the citation must be worded as invention and development, not as sole origin. Eriksson and Johansson are right that precision of an established technique is a different kind of advance from a new class of matter, and B028 has the broadest opening support and the longest confirmation record. Choosing B034 means the committee prefers clean credit and demonstrated reproducibility to conceptual breadth, and I accept that this is a judgement and not a proof.

responses.point: Kroll asked who made the first statistically decisive IceCube observation and said a single-name B005 prize needs an explicit rationale, while preferring the clock as a single clean prize.
responses.response: Your question is fair and I cannot answer it within one name. The 2013 diffuse-flux observation was an analysis by the collaboration, not a result that can be assigned to Halzen alone, and AMANDA, the construction effort and the analysis leaders are all outside the credit. I therefore drop the B005 part and keep the clock alone, which is the single-prize form you and Lindroth proposed. On your disclosure, I think transparency is sufficient for a candidate whose credit rests on the published record and is reproduced by several laboratories, but I would like the committee record to show it, and I would not ask you to lead the drafting of the B034 citation.

responses.point: Danielsson judged a one-laureate prize for a large collaboration too fragile for this round, although he ranked B005 second and values the observable, and he named B034 as his best fallback if B028 allocation is judged too contested.
responses.response: I accept your assessment of B005 and it is the main reason I withdraw it. I value that you keep B034 as the fallback, and I note that you and Mehlig do not agree that the pending redefinition of the second adds merit. I agree, and I no longer lean on it. My case for the clock rests on what was demonstrated and reproduced. On B028 we agree on Kane and Mele; my remaining difficulty is not the topological-insulator science but that every three-name set leaves a strong claimant out (Hasan, or Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang), whereas the clock pair has no internal exclusion.

responses.point: Johansson holds that B028 created a new class of quantum matter whereas B034 advances the precision of an established technique, and asks whether the overlap with the 2005 comb prize weakens the novelty of B034.
responses.response: I take the distinction seriously: B028 is the larger conceptual reorganisation. I would answer in two parts. First, the 2005 prize recognised the comb as a tool for measuring optical frequencies, and the 2012 prize recognised control of single trapped ions; neither contains the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice, which is why the clock reached 10^-18 stability through large atom numbers. Second, the Nobel will also names inventions, and this is a new method, not a refinement of a known one. I do not think that clean attribution is greater merit, but when two candidates are close in merit I think it is a legitimate reason to prefer the one whose credit can be defended in full.

responses.point: Eriksson holds that B034 is more an instrument achievement than a new regime of matter, that the fundamental-physics results it should enable have not yet arrived, and that he would not block it.
responses.response: As someone who builds instruments I do not regard that as a lesser category, but I accept your point that the strongest fundamental-physics payoffs (new constraints on constants, a redefined second) are still to come. I would argue that the prize does not need them: the demonstrated result is a measurement at 10^-18 reproduced independently, which has already been used for relativistic geodesy comparisons and for bounds on variation of constants. I also take your point that B028 is more mature than B046 and that you could recognise B028 first; that is a coherent order, and it is the same as my alternatives.

responses.point: Lindroth supports B034 on atomic-structure grounds, takes the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes seriously but narrowly, and holds that the discovery does not hinge on the pending redefinition of the second.
responses.response: Your atomic-structure argument is the one I would use against the overlap objection: the control of polarizability, multipole and blackbody shifts is the physics that made 10^-18 reachable, so the achievement is not a repetition of the comb. I agree that the discovery does not hinge on the redefinition and that waiting for metrology bodies would hand the decision to them. On my earlier question, your answer on B002 is accepted and the B005 credit problem is, if anything, worse, so I drop both and do not pair the clock with another part.

responses.point: Olsson names B034 as the cleaner configuration if credit on B028 is judged to misstate the original work, and says nothing forces the clocks to be decided this year.
responses.response: I agree that B034 is the natural fallback for B028 and I accept the argument that waiting is legitimate. My reason for preferring to decide it now is that the result is already reproduced at 10^-18 across independent laboratories, and I would not want the prize to depend on an administrative date. If the committee judges that the B028 trio is credible, I would not oppose B028 on science; my objection is only that omitting Hasan or Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang makes the attribution contested in a way the clock credit is not.

uncertainties: Whether other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Bloom) have priority claims strong enough to change a Katori and Ye credit, which I cannot verify from the supplied record.
How much the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 trapped-ion prize should weigh against novelty; I regard the magic-wavelength lattice as distinct but the committee may disagree.
Whether the committee prefers B028 for conceptual breadth despite the allocation problem, in which case my position would move to B028 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.
Whether neutrino astronomy can be recognised in a later year with a credited set that represents the collaboration, which this ballot cannot support.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal issue is apparent from my profile for B034, B028 or B046. My field is astroparticle instrumentation (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) and I have no recorded tie to Katori, Ye or the other credited names. I withdraw B005 from my configuration and record no IceCube link. The gamma-ray burst afterglow candidate B004 remains adjacent to my gamma-ray burst instrumentation interests, and I would not take a lead role on it. I have noted Kroll's disclosed link to the Hall laboratory environment and regard it as something to record for the committee, not as a bar to discussion.
